summary: Verified the ref (Schinzel, Funct. Approx. 28 (2000) 187–194, projecteuclid) and did the short proof attempt for fixed-a families n = m² − a: whenever a = d·e with d ≡ e (mod 2) and (e−d)/2 odd, the INTEGER m0 = (d+e)/2 makes m0² − a = ((e−d)/2)² an odd square, and adelically (Hensel at odd ℓ, n ≡ 1 mod 8 at 2) a square-mimicking m exists for every a in the n ≡ 1 (4) classes; so any polynomial-in-m Type I/II identity cover of {m² − a} is killed by T1 exactly as Mordell–Schinzel (B1 Thm M, POINTWISE_SIZE.md §1–4). Partial-class identities for n = (Mk+r)² − a exist trivially (B,C const, u quadratic: (4BC−1) | m² − a + B), but each a covers density 0; letting a = p − ⌊√p⌋² vary is an unbounded p-dependent search (E1/E2 in POINTWISE_SIZE §4), with no structure gained from √.
evidence: POINTWISE_SIZE.md §1 Thm M, §4 scope (⌊√r⌋ is an E2 primitive)

summary: Computed, for fixed p, the set of winning (★) levels C (∃ u,B: 4uBC−u−B = p; scripts/z52b_p1_H04_winC.py): it is finite (C ≤ (p+1)/4 − ish) and log-uniformly spread, e.g. p = 9999937: C ∈ {1,2,6,10,11,18,26,35,62,101,452,510,692,8993,9058}; p = 99990001: 14 winners up to C = 1785536 with max gap 1.3·10⁶; p = 409: none. So 'good C' is not syndetic/thick/IP in any sense (≍ log²p points in [1, p/4] with density ∝ 1/C), and there is no recurrence/minimal-system structure to exploit; the Furstenberg correspondence only addresses positive-density sets, which neither the winner set nor the failure set is.

The premise is vacuous: for a prime p ≡ 1 (mod 4) the Type I slice f | p² + 4c²d, f ≡ −p (mod 4cd) is EMPTY whenever d is a square (PROVED, one line: p² + (2cs)² with gcd(p, 2cs) ∈ {1, p} has only prime factors ≡ 1 mod 4, so every divisor is ≡ 1 mod 4 ≠ −p ≡ 3 mod 4); a Type I certificate needs a prime q ≡ 3 (4) with (d/q) = −1, so d must be a non-square. Confirmed by brute force (0 hits in 24 687 (p, c, d ∈ {1, 4, 9}) tests for p < 3000, versus 202/211 primes hit with d ∈ {2,3,5,6,7}), and the C run over p ≤ 10⁶, c ≤ 10⁴ found no d = 1 certificate at all (killed at the time box). The 'Gaussian-integer sub-problem' is therefore not a sub-problem of ES; the sum-of-two-squares structure acts only as the trivial obstruction.

The 2-bridge/rational-tangle dictionary (ES₅(p) ⟺ some K(p/A) with (A/p) = −1 bounds a 3-band plumbing) is already BRAINSTORM/bsA_lens_homotopy_surgery.md P3. New cheap step: for p ≡ 1 (4) < 700 compared the Murasugi-sum signature of K(p/A) with the HJ length r(p/A) (scripts/z52b_p1_H04_tangle_sig.py): length ≤ 3 words occur at signatures spread over 0…224 for both residue symbols (e.g. r = 3: 182 non-residue vs 50 residue words at σ = 0, 4 vs 2 at σ = 116), and (r(p/A), r(p/(p−A))) does not determine σ (614 of 1445 pairs ambiguous) — no signature threshold encodes 'length ≤ 3', and σ is blind to the ES bit. The alt step (tangle sum as a composition law) fails structurally: the sum of two rational tangles is rational only if one is integral, so it yields Montesinos links, not ES₅ words of related numerators.

Exactly BRAINSTORM/bsA_lens_homotopy_surgery.md P1 (Whitehead homotopy dictionary: ES₅(p) ⟺ a non-L(p,1)-homotopy-type lens space of order p bounds a ≤3-sphere linear plumbing), P2 (Greene's realisation/changemaker theorem only covers the QR side, so certificates lie where it is silent), P4 (Matveev complexity) and the T1 scope check at squares; λ(p) tabulation exists (scripts/bsA_hjlen.py). d-invariants/Casson–Walker are obstructions to fillings, not existence results for short plumbings (memo's barrier screen); nothing new in the item.

Exact (★) counts R(n) for all n ≤ 2·10⁷ (scripts/z52b_p1_H04_rstar.c, 2 s); on the 86 families n = k·m² / k·m⁴ (k ≤ 200 non-square, n ≡ 1 mod 4, 10³ ≤ n ≤ 2·10⁷) there are 7 zeros of R in total vs 5.7 expected from controls matched by class mod 840 and size (largest excess k = 33: 3 vs 1.3 — 1617, 40425, 66825, all with small factors), so no hidden square-class/quartic family obstruction beyond T1 for (★). The 14 (★) prime failures ≤ 2·10⁷ (409 … 8813281, matching the repo census) are all ≡ 1 (mod 8) (forced by Mordell-hardness, so (−1/p)₄ = 1 trivially), with (2/p)₄ = +1 for 9/14 and (3/p)₄ = +1 for 7/14 — consistent with coin flips.

The item's own first step resolves to known repo content: the twisted divisor sum σ_χ(N) = Σ_{d|N} χ(d) = Π_{q^e∥N}(1 + χ(q) + … + χ(q)^e) is an Eisenstein coefficient (no Waldspurger/toric period needed, it vanishes iff some q^e∥N has χ(q) = −1, e odd), and FRONTIER §2.3 (METAPLECTIC_ES Thm K) already writes every level series as a Kronecker theta quotient (odd χ) plus even-character divisor sums with 'no cusp forms', while §2.4 gives M_t^lev(n) = (τ(N) − σ_{χ_{−t}}(N))/φ(t) ≥ 0 and its pointwise positivity at non-squares (SYNTHESIS_SPARKS9 Prop 2.2). The remaining event (divisor in the single class −1 inside the χ_{−t} = −1 coset) involves all characters mod 4C, i.e. a single-integer competition no single L-value controls; BRAINSTORM/bsB_theta_multiplier.md ran the Waldspurger/Shimura screen and refuted the eigenform-coefficient reading numerically (no zero propagation along square classes).

The LLL/Shearer/Janson placement-of-randomness analysis at fixed p is BRAINSTORM/prob_lll_fixed_p.md (verdict: collapses to B2/B1/B6), and the 'integer C-form statement' is the zero law of FRONTIER §2.4 on odd non-squares. Checked the item's proposed integer conjecture with exact R(n), n ≤ 2·10⁷: it is FALSE — 860 odd non-squares have no (★)/C-form certificate (345 ≡ 1, 515 ≡ 3 mod 4; 836 composites, 708 divisible by 3, e.g. 15, 39, 105, …, 19897095), so primality (or at least more than non-squareness) matters and the right integer statement is ES itself via prime factors. Curiosity only (n ≡ 3 mod 4, ES-trivial): the 3-mod-4 prime zeros include the Mersenne primes 3, 7, 31, 127, 8191.

Short proof attempt of the game's structure: with move 'subtract 1/x keeping r ≥ 0' and 'whoever reaches 0 wins', a position r is an immediate win iff r is a unit fraction, and from any non-unit r the mover can always choose x so large that r − 1/x is not a unit fraction (two consecutive unit fractions differ by 1/(x(x+1)), so at most one huge x per gap is bad), so the opponent can always stall — the game has no P/N structure tied to ES (plays need not terminate; with a 3-move cap the answer is determined by move parity, not by representability). ES is the 1-player (solitaire) 'reach 0 in 3 moves' statement, i.e. itself; a web search ('Egyptian fraction game subtract unit fractions Sprague-Grundy') found only recreational pages, no structural result.
evidence: web search 2026-10-31 (NRICH / Wikipedia Egyptian fraction hits only)

summary: Ran the comparison for C ≤ 30 on all 108 397 primes p ≡ 1 (4) in [10⁸, 1.04·10⁸] (scripts/z52b_p1_H04_pdmodel.c, data/z52b/pass1/H04/pdmodel.txt): empirical per-level failure P(no d | 4Cp+1, d ≡ −1 mod 4C) rises 0.206 (C=1), 0.426 (C=2) … 0.938 (C=30). The item's model (actual factorisation shapes, i.i.d. uniform classes in (ℤ/4C)^×) is badly off (0.157, 0.271 … 0.829: it ignores that the class product is forced ≡ N ≡ 1), while conditioning the classes on product ≡ 1 matches to ±0.03 for C ≥ 2 (0.469 vs 0.426, 0.922 vs 0.938 at C=30) but overestimates C=1 (0.316 vs 0.206); integers n instead of primes fail more (0.286 at C=1: primes p make 4Cp+1 divisible by small ℓ with prob 1/(ℓ−1) not 1/ℓ). So the 'principled per-level probability' is just the Erdős–Rényi/subset-product model already used in FORCED_WINDOW §4, needs the product constraint, and says nothing about the joint (all-level) lower tail, which is the actual question (FRONTIER §2.4 zero law).

Histogrammed t = log d/log N over all 1 079 432 (★) certificates (4uC−1)(4BC−1) = 4Cp+1 of primes p ≡ 1 (4) ≤ 10⁶ (scripts/z52b_p1_H04_benford.c, data/z52b/pass1/H04/benford.txt). At fixed small level (C < 10) t is flat (≈0.060 per 0.05-bin on [0.05, 0.95]) — the hyperbola/pair-count law, not arcsine (arcsine is the random-divisor-of-random-integer law with 1/τ weights; all divisors of the same N give the expected near-arcsine-minus-ends shape); pooled over C the mass concentrates at t ≈ ½ (0.13 per bin at 0.45–0.55) purely because d ≡ −1 (mod 4C) forces d ≥ 4C − 1, i.e. t ≥ log 4C/log(4Cp), and large C dominates the count (C ≥ 1000: 32% of mass in each central bin). No residue-induced size bias beyond this forced cutoff; nothing for weights or Lenstra-type large-modulus arguments.

summary: The Hooley/Kummer-field analogy has been run in the repo: CONDITIONAL_ES.md §3.2 (ES witness conditions ℓ | N are ramification, not Frobenius, conditions; Frobenius in ℚ(ζ_M, √p) gives (ℓ mod M, (p/ℓ)), not p mod ℓ; under GRH only ck_min ≫ log p log log p i.o.) and BALANCED_LATTICE.md §2 item 1 ('the brief's Hooley/Kummer route certifies only the index condition plus a negligible fraction of characters', Prop 2.2/2.4 PROVED/Assessment), with (J)98 giving only M_gen(p) ≥ (1 − o(1)) log log p on GRH. Additionally the item's concrete first step is vacuous: the Type I d = 1 slice (p + 2ci) has NO certificates for p ≡ 1 (4) (all divisors of p² + 4c² are ≡ 1 mod 4 ≠ −p; see Z1482 in this batch). The shape mismatch is the tied modulus: Artin has a fixed base a and an independent varying prime modulus (density via Chebotarev), ES has moduli 4C tied to the integer 4Cp+1 being factored.

Verified the restatement (#E(F_q) = q+1 for y² = x³ − x at all primes q ≡ 3 (4) < 3000; scripts/z52b_p1_H04_cm.py), so a PRIME certificate q | 4Cp+1 is exactly 4C | #E(F_q). But it does not extend: composite certificates d ≡ −1 (mod 4C) need not have any prime factor ≡ ±1 (mod 4C) and #E is not multiplicative over d, and 'q ≡ −1 mod 4C' is just 'Frob_q = complex conjugation in ℚ(ζ_{4C})' (BRAINSTORM/bsD_artin_conjugation.md), which the CM curve re-encodes through E[4C] ⊂ ℚ(ζ_{4C})-ish torsion. The ECM idea fails: [k]P ≡ O (mod q) detects ord(P) | k, i.e. smoothness of q+1 (Williams p+1), not the divisibility 4C | q+1 with unknown cofactor, so it is no faster than factoring 4Cp+1; the Koblitz/Zywina machinery counts primes with prescribed #E-properties, not divisors of a prescribed integer.

Wrote the lemma (PROVED, classical): prime divisors q ∤ D of a value primitively represented by a form of discriminant D satisfy χ_D(q) = 1, so modulo 4C they lie in ker χ_D (index 2) when cond(χ_D) | 4C and are unconstrained otherwise; cyclotomic Φ_m gives the subgroup {1 mod m}. Rigidity therefore yields subgroups, never the coset −1. Tabulation: ker χ_D = {±1} ⊂ (ℤ/4C)^× needs φ(4C) = 4, i.e. only C = 2 (D = 8, x² − 2y², primes ≡ ±1 mod 8) and C = 3 (D = +12, x² − 3y², primes ≡ ±1 mod 12; the item's x² + 3 is D = −12, the wrong character); in both cases, when 4Cp+1 is such a value, a certificate exists iff some prime factor is ≡ −1, and since the count of such factors is merely even (N ≡ 1), nothing is forced — the 'parity escape' is empty.
evidence: Cox, Primes of the form x² + ny², §2 (genus characters)

summary: Primary-source check via Graham, 'Paul Erdős and Egyptian fractions' (UCSD PDF, §2) and Bloom–Elsholtz, NAW 5/23 (2022) 237: the conjecture's only early written source is Erdős, Mat. Lapok 1 (1950) 192–210 ('attributed to himself and Ernst G. Straus'; 'it is unknown when the conjecture was originally made'), plus Obláth's 1950 note; Graham even remarks it is curious Erdős–Straus did not also pose the 5/n analogue. No Straus paper on 4/n, and no Straus-favoured heuristic or partial result, appears in either survey's bibliography; Straus's unit-fraction work with Erdős is on irrationality of Ahmes series, unrelated to ES's mechanism.

Two cheap checks. (i) T1 reaches every (u,v)-class: primitive Pythagorean pairs hit only 3072 of the 12288 classes (u0,v0) mod 840 able to carry Mordell-hard primes (2-adic: u ≡ 0, v ≡ 3 mod 8 is impossible for primitive triples), but unit multiples k·(u,v,w) — still with u² + v² = (kw)² an odd square — hit all 12288 (and all 49152 mod 1680) (scripts/z52b_p1_H04_pyth.py), so every congruence region of (u,v) contains odd-square points in every direction. (ii) Proof sketch (not reviewed) for the ET Type II shape 4abd = n + e, ce = a + b with a, b, c, d, e ∈ ℚ[u,v]: since u² + v² + (linear) never factors over ℚ (definite quadratic part), a degree count forces e constant with two of a, b, d constant, or e = (n + 4b²d)/(4bcd − 1) — integrality is then a congruence on n = u² + v² alone, i.e. back to Mordell covering (B1); Type I has a similar but messier count (Assessment). So identities 'polynomial in (u,v)' gain nothing over identities in n.
evidence: POINTWISE_SIZE.md Thm M (two-squares decomposition is an E2 primitive, so not formally covered there)

summary: Classified all 18 834 (★) level failures for 200 Mordell-hard primes in [1.0006·10⁶, 1.087·10⁶] and C ≤ 100 (1166 levels hit; scripts/z52b_p1_H04_kneser.py, data/z52b/pass1/H04/kneser.txt): 76% are subgroup obstructions (−1 ∉ ⟨classes of the prime factors of 4Cp+1⟩, i.e. too few/too aligned primes), 24% have −1 in that subgroup but not in the divisor set D (|D|/|⟨primes⟩| median 0.21). The Kneser stabiliser of D is trivial in 84% of failures (non-periodic D), so the periodic/non-periodic dichotomy adds no usable structure: failures are just 'small ω(N)'. Consistent with BRAINSTORM/z31_zero_sum.md (Kneser/Davenport lengths never met by a forced N; at windows subgroup membership is even forced by reciprocity, CAP_POINTWISE Thm 1.1, while at (★) levels it is the dominant failure mode).

BRAINSTORM/other_rings.md Prop 3.3 (PROVED) already shows totally positive ES over O_K for every real quadratic K with N(ε) = −1 (incl. ℚ(√5)) for all rational n ≥ 2, via a totally positive unit η = ε^{2j} ≡ −1 (mod ℓ) for an inert ℓ ≡ 3 (4) — the 'thick unit reservoir' the item predicts; it also explains why it is useless for ℤ (it uses totally positive elements < 1 at one place, which ℕ lacks; no T1, since inv_{σ₁} + inv_{σ₂} = 0, T1_TEMPLATE.md §1). The item's first step (find a reformulation 'ES(p) ⟸ representation of a p-dependent integer by a FIXED ternary form' and record why each fails) is done in the repo: BRAINSTORM/bsD_genus_vacuity_LDp.md Prop 1/Remark 2 (quaternion/Gross-lattice ternary reformulation: genus is vacuous; Duke–Schulze-Pillot controls only the represented number, while the certificate needs the isometry class of v^⊥ — a mixed-equidistribution, O(1)-on-average lottery), B2_ACROSS_FIELDS.md §3 row 3 and §4.3 (ternary/Duke: Eisenstein main term ≍ n^{1/2} vs polylog certificate count, ES condition on a representative dividing a prescribed element; verdict ANALOGUE, NOT SHARP), and FRONTIER B5 (T1: every 'local + spinor ⇒ global' route is false at odd squares, where all local/genus/spinor conditions hold). No fixed-form reformulation exists in the repo's ternary memos — the forms move with p (B2/B3).

Wrote the 'Helfgott target' table from FRONTIER §§2.2–2.4/§5: the only unconditional asymptotics at a single p are main-term bounds (M_BM(p) ≥ (3/(16π²) − o(1)) log²p via Burgess; ES₅ M(p) ≥ (45/(32π²) − o(1))L²), whose o(1) could be made explicit with explicit Burgess (Treviño-type) constants — but no unconditional or standard-conjecture-conditional lower bound for R(p), f_I(p), f_II(p) or λ(p) ≤ 3 exists at all (§2.4: no implication from GRH/GLH/EH/BFI/Montgomery is known; H⁻_BM(ε, p₀) is 'ES-(★) in disguise'). Note that for H⁻_BM the constant is irrelevant: R ∈ ℤ and ε·M_BM > 0 already give R ≥ 1, so with p₀ = 10¹⁸ (verification) any ε > 0 suffices — the Vinogradov→Helfgott move (shrink an existing effective threshold) has no asymptotic theorem to start from; the gap is qualitative, not a constant.

INVOLUTION_ES2.md already bars finite-menu affine windmills (Cor 6.2 under Bateman–Horn; unconditional except Siegel cylinders), so only the item's empirical parity step was new. Exhaustive solution counts for all 273 Mordell-hard primes ≤ 10⁵ (scripts/z52b_p1_H04_parity.c, data/z52b/pass1/H04/parity.txt): f(p) is odd at 127/273, f_I at 128, f_II at 139 — coin flips; there are no fixed points of the natural coordinate involutions at all (#{y = z} = #{x = y} = 0 at every hard prime), so the Zagier mechanism ('the other involution has exactly one fixed point') has nothing to count for the obvious symmetries. No natural restricted count with constant parity appeared; a parity route would need a non-affine/n-dependent involution (INVOLUTION_ES2 §7 residue).

Singularity type is immediate (and already in the repo): 4xyz = nw(xy+yz+zx) ⟺ 1/x + 1/y + 1/z + 1/w′ = 0 with w′ = −nw/4, i.e. the closure is Cayley's 4-nodal (4A₁) cubic over ℚ for every n, nodes at the four coordinate points (BRAINSTORM/cayley_markoff_cm.md P1, scripts/bs_cubic_cayley.py). Heath-Brown's universal torsor X_i = ε y_j y_k y_l z_ij z_ik z_il (2003, Lemma 1; N(B) ≍ B(log B)⁶) and the fact that ET's Type I/II parameters ARE torsor coordinates (ET Remark 2.10) are recorded in BRAINSTORM/graph_cayley_moves.md §2; restricting to the fibre y₃ = −n leaves exactly the ET divisor problem (one coordinate fixed = the tied-modulus B2 event), so the torsor count is a global height asymptotic, not a pointwise statement (cf. BRAINSTORM/z52_lit_points_automorphic.md on integral-point torsor counts).
